title: Standard Form (Deeper)
description: Calculating with numbers in standard index form — multiplication, division, addition and subtraction without a calculator.

notes.heading: Multiplying Numbers in Standard Form
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To multiply two numbers written in standard form, deal with the coefficients and the powers of $10$ separately:
$$(a \times 10^m) \times (b \times 10^n) = (a \times b) \times 10^{m+n}$$

🔑 How it works
1. Multiply the two coefficients (the numbers between $1$ and $10$).
2. Multiply the powers of $10$ by ADDING the indices.
3. If the new coefficient is not between $1$ and $10$, adjust the answer back into standard form.

💡 Worked Example 1
Simplify $(4 \times 10^5) \times (3 \times 10^3)$.

• Coefficients: $4 \times 3 = 12$
• Powers: $10^5 \times 10^3 = 10^{5+3} = 10^8$
• Result so far: $12 \times 10^8$ — not standard form, because $12 \geq 10$.

Adjust: $12 = 1.2 \times 10$, so
$$12 \times 10^8 = 1.2 \times 10^9$$

💡 Worked Example 2
Simplify $(7 \times 10^{-9}) \times (8 \times 10^{20})$.

• Coefficients: $7 \times 8 = 56$
• Powers: $10^{-9} \times 10^{20} = 10^{-9+20} = 10^{11}$
• Result so far: $56 \times 10^{11}$ — again too big a coefficient.

Adjust: $56 = 5.6 \times 10$, so
$$56 \times 10^{11} = 5.6 \times 10^{12}$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Multiply coefficients, ADD indices.
• The index laws work with negative indices too: $-9 + 20 = 11$.
• The final answer is not finished until the coefficient satisfies $1 \leq a < 10$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Adding the coefficients instead of multiplying them. $(4 \times 10^5) \times (3 \times 10^3)$ is not $7 \times 10^8$ — the coefficients are multiplied: $4 \times 3 = 12$.

notes.heading: Dividing Numbers in Standard Form
notes.body:
📌 Definition
To divide two numbers in standard form, divide the coefficients and divide the powers of $10$ by SUBTRACTING the indices:
$$(a \times 10^m) \div (b \times 10^n) = \left(\dfrac{a}{b}\right) \times 10^{m-n}$$

🔑 How it works
1. Write the division as a fraction if it helps.
2. Divide the coefficients.
3. Subtract the indices of the powers of $10$.
4. Adjust the result into standard form if the coefficient is not between $1$ and $10$.

💡 Worked Example 1
Simplify $(9 \times 10^6) \div (4 \times 10^2)$.

• Coefficients: $9 \div 4 = 2.25$
• Powers: $10^6 \div 10^2 = 10^{6-2} = 10^4$

$$\dfrac{9 \times 10^6}{4 \times 10^2} = 2.25 \times 10^4$$
The coefficient $2.25$ is already between $1$ and $10$, so no adjustment is needed.

💡 Worked Example 2
Simplify $(6 \times 10^7) \div (8 \times 10^{-2})$.

• Coefficients: $6 \div 8 = 0.75$
• Powers: $10^{7-(-2)} = 10^{7+2} = 10^9$
• Result so far: $0.75 \times 10^9$ — not standard form, because $0.75 < 1$.

Adjust: $0.75 \times 10 = 7.5$, so
$$0.75 \times 10^9 = 7.5 \times 10^8$$

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Divide coefficients, SUBTRACT indices.
• Subtracting a negative index means adding: $7 - (-2) = 9$.
• A coefficient below $1$ must be fixed by moving the decimal point and lowering the index.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Adding the indices during division. $10^6 \div 10^2 = 10^4$, not $10^8$. Multiplication adds indices; division subtracts them.

notes.heading: Adjusting an Answer into Standard Form
notes.body:
📌 Definition
After a multiplication or division, the coefficient often ends up outside the allowed range $1 \leq a < 10$. Adjusting means rewriting the number so the coefficient is back in range, by shifting value between the coefficient and the power of $10$.

🔑 How it works
• If the coefficient is TOO BIG ($a \geq 10$): divide it by $10$ and add $1$ to the index.
• If the coefficient is TOO SMALL ($a < 1$): multiply it by $10$ and subtract $1$ from the index.

The value never changes — you are only moving a factor of $10$ from one part to the other.

💡 Worked Example 1 — coefficient too big
Write $25 \times 10^6$ in standard form.

$25 = 2.5 \times 10^1$, so
$$25 \times 10^6 = 2.5 \times 10^1 \times 10^6 = 2.5 \times 10^7$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — coefficient too small
Write $0.4 \times 10^{-5}$ in standard form.

$0.4 = 4 \times 10^{-1}$, so
$$0.4 \times 10^{-5} = 4 \times 10^{-1} \times 10^{-5} = 4 \times 10^{-6}$$

💡 Worked Example 3 — chained adjustment
$56 \times 10^{11} = 5.6 \times 10 \times 10^{11} = 5.6 \times 10^{12}$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Coefficient too big → index goes UP by $1$.
• Coefficient too small → index goes DOWN by $1$.
• Always do this adjustment as the LAST step of a calculation.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Moving the index the wrong way. $25 \times 10^6$ is $2.5 \times 10^7$, not $2.5 \times 10^5$. Shrinking the coefficient by a factor of $10$ must be balanced by growing the power by a factor of $10$.

✅ Check
Convert both versions to an ordinary number: $25 \times 10^6 = 25\,000\,000$ and $2.5 \times 10^7 = 25\,000\,000$. They match.

notes.heading: Working with Negative Indices
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Small numbers use negative indices in standard form. The index laws apply to them in exactly the same way: add indices when multiplying, subtract when dividing — using normal negative number arithmetic.

🔑 How it works
• $10^{-4} \times 10^{-7} = 10^{-4+(-7)} = 10^{-11}$
• $10^{-3} \div 10^{-9} = 10^{-3-(-9)} = 10^{6}$

Remember the sign rules:
• Adding a negative: $-4 + (-7) = -11$
• Subtracting a negative: $-3 - (-9) = -3 + 9 = 6$

💡 Worked Example 1 — multiplying small numbers
Simplify $(5 \times 10^{-4}) \times (6 \times 10^{-7})$.

• Coefficients: $5 \times 6 = 30$
• Powers: $10^{-4+(-7)} = 10^{-11}$
• Result: $30 \times 10^{-11}$, which adjusts to
$$3 \times 10^{-10}$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — dividing small numbers
Simplify $(8 \times 10^{-3}) \div (2 \times 10^{-9})$.

• Coefficients: $8 \div 2 = 4$
• Powers: $10^{-3-(-9)} = 10^6$

$$\dfrac{8 \times 10^{-3}}{2 \times 10^{-9}} = 4 \times 10^6$$
The answer is a LARGE number — dividing by a very small number gives a large result.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Negative indices follow the same add/subtract index laws.
• A negative index does not make the value negative; it makes it small.
• Dividing by $10^{-9}$ is the same as multiplying by $10^9$.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Getting the sign wrong when subtracting a negative index. $-3 - (-9) = 6$, not $-12$. Rewrite it as $-3 + 9$ before you calculate.

notes.heading: Adding and Subtracting in Standard Form
notes.body:
📌 Definition
You cannot add or subtract numbers in standard form while their powers of $10$ are different. First rewrite both numbers with the SAME power of $10$, then add or subtract the coefficients.

🔑 How it works
1. Choose the larger power of $10$.
2. Rewrite the other number using that power (its coefficient will get smaller).
3. Add or subtract the coefficients.
4. Check the answer is in standard form; adjust if needed.

💡 Worked Example 1 — adding
Simplify $(4.6 \times 10^7) + (3.2 \times 10^6)$.

Rewrite $3.2 \times 10^6$ with the power $10^7$:
$$3.2 \times 10^6 = 0.32 \times 10^7$$
Now add the coefficients:
$$(4.6 + 0.32) \times 10^7 = 4.92 \times 10^7$$

💡 Worked Example 2 — subtracting
Simplify $(8 \times 10^{-3}) - (5 \times 10^{-4})$.

Rewrite $5 \times 10^{-4}$ with the power $10^{-3}$:
$$5 \times 10^{-4} = 0.5 \times 10^{-3}$$
Now subtract:
$$(8 - 0.5) \times 10^{-3} = 7.5 \times 10^{-3}$$

✅ Check
$8 \times 10^{-3} = 0.008$ and $5 \times 10^{-4} = 0.0005$.
$0.008 - 0.0005 = 0.0075 = 7.5 \times 10^{-3}$. Correct.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Equal powers first, then combine the coefficients.
• Converting to the LARGER power keeps the other coefficient simple (usually just one decimal shift).
• You can always check by converting to ordinary numbers.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Adding coefficients with different powers: $(4 \times 10^5) + (3 \times 10^4) \neq 7 \times 10^9$ and it is not $7 \times 10^5$ either. It is $4.3 \times 10^5$, because $3 \times 10^4 = 0.3 \times 10^5$.

notes.heading: Standard Form in Real-World Problems
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Science, technology and finance all use standard form to handle extremely large or small quantities — distances across space, nanotechnology sizes, national budgets. The calculation rules are the same; the skill is extracting the numbers and giving the answer in standard form.

🔑 How it works
1. Read the problem and identify the operation (How many times bigger? Total? Share equally?).
2. Write every quantity in standard form.
3. Apply the multiply/divide/add/subtract rules.
4. Adjust the final answer into standard form and include units.

💡 Worked Example 1 — area
A rectangular solar farm is $4 \times 10^3$ m long and $2.5 \times 10^2$ m wide. Find its area.

$$(4 \times 10^3) \times (2.5 \times 10^2) = (4 \times 2.5) \times 10^{3+2} = 10 \times 10^5$$
Adjust: $10 \times 10^5 = 1 \times 10^6$ m$^2$.

💡 Worked Example 2 — sharing a budget
A government spends £6 \times 10^9 on a scheme shared equally among $3 \times 10^7$ people. How much is that per person?

$$\dfrac{6 \times 10^9}{3 \times 10^7} = (6 \div 3) \times 10^{9-7} = 2 \times 10^2$$
That is £200 per person.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Units belong with the final answer: m$^2$, £, km.
• "How many times bigger" means divide.
• Always adjust the coefficient into the range $1 \leq a < 10$ at the end.

⚠️ Common Mistake
Stopping at $10 \times 10^5$. A coefficient of $10$ is not allowed — adjust to $1 \times 10^6$.

notes.heading: Estimating, Comparing and Common Errors
notes.body:
📌 Definition
Standard form is a powerful estimating tool: round each awkward number to $1$ significant figure, convert to standard form, and the index laws make the mental arithmetic easy.

🔑 How it works
1. Round each number to $1$ significant figure.
2. Write each rounded value in standard form.
3. Use the multiplication/division rules for a quick estimate.

💡 Worked Example — estimating
Estimate $0.000\,078 \times 6\,500\,000$.

• $0.000\,078 \approx 8 \times 10^{-5}$
• $6\,500\,000 \approx 7 \times 10^6$

$$(8 \times 10^{-5}) \times (7 \times 10^6) = 56 \times 10^1 = 5.6 \times 10^2 \approx 560$$
The exact value is $507$, so $560$ is a sensible estimate.

🔑 Comparing sizes
To compare two numbers in standard form, compare the powers of $10$ first — the bigger power always wins. Only if the powers are equal do you compare coefficients.

Example: $4 \times 10^{-5}$ versus $9 \times 10^{-6}$.
Since $-5 > -6$, the number $4 \times 10^{-5} = 0.000\,04$ is larger than $9 \times 10^{-6} = 0.000\,009$ — even though $9 > 4$.

📎 Key Points to Remember
• Multiply: coefficients multiply, indices ADD.
• Divide: coefficients divide, indices SUBTRACT.
• Add/subtract: equal powers first, then combine coefficients.
• Finish every answer with a coefficient between $1$ and $10$.

⚠️ Common Mistakes — summary
• Adding coefficients when multiplying, or adding indices when dividing.
• Forgetting to adjust answers like $56 \times 10^{11}$ into $5.6 \times 10^{12}$.
• Adding numbers whose powers of $10$ differ without converting first.
• Mishandling double negatives in indices, e.g. $-3 - (-9)$.

✅ Check
Convert your final answer to an ordinary number and compare it with a rough estimate. If they are wildly different, find the slip.

flashcards.term: Adjusting a coefficient that is too big
flashcards.definition: If the coefficient is $10$ or more, divide it by $10$ and add $1$ to the index.

flashcards.term: Adjusting a coefficient that is too small
flashcards.definition: If the coefficient is less than $1$, multiply it by $10$ and subtract $1$ from the index.
Rewrite both numbers with the same power of $10$, then add the coefficients.

The index laws still apply: $10^a \times 10^b = 10^{a+b}$ even when $a$ or $b$ is negative.
Subtracting a negative index means adding its value, because two minuses make a plus.
When adding or subtracting, rewrite the smaller-power number with the larger power; its coefficient shifts one decimal place per index step.

questions.stem: Simplify $(3 \times 10^4) \times (2 \times 10^5)$, giving your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: Multiply the coefficients ($3 \times 2 = 6$) and add the indices ($4 + 5 = 9$), giving $6 \times 10^9$. The coefficient is already between $1$ and $10$.

questions.stem: Simplify $(5 \times 10^6) \times (4 \times 10^3)$, giving your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: $5 \times 4 = 20$ and $6 + 3 = 9$, giving $20 \times 10^9$. Since $20 = 2 \times 10$, the answer adjusts to $2 \times 10^{10}$.

questions.stem: Simplify $(7 \times 10^{-9}) \times (8 \times 10^{20})$, giving your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: $7 \times 8 = 56$ and $-9 + 20 = 11$, giving $56 \times 10^{11}$. Adjusting the coefficient gives $5.6 \times 10^{12}$; the option $5.6 \times 10^{11}$ forgets this adjustment.

questions.stem: Simplify $(9 \times 10^8) \div (3 \times 10^5)$, giving your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: Divide the coefficients ($9 \div 3 = 3$) and subtract the indices ($8 - 5 = 3$), giving $3 \times 10^3$. Adding the indices would wrongly give $10^{13}$.

questions.stem: Simplify $(6 \times 10^7) \div (8 \times 10^{-2})$, giving your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: $6 \div 8 = 0.75$ and $7 - (-2) = 9$, giving $0.75 \times 10^9$. Since $0.75 < 1$, adjust to $7.5 \times 10^8$. The option $7.5 \times 10^9$ skips this adjustment.

questions.stem: Simplify $(8 \times 10^{-3}) \div (2 \times 10^{-9})$, giving your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: $8 \div 2 = 4$ and $-3 - (-9) = -3 + 9 = 6$, so the answer is $4 \times 10^6$. Dividing by a very small number gives a large answer.

questions.stem: Which of these is $34 \times 10^6$ written correctly in standard form?
questions.explanation: $34 = 3.4 \times 10$, so $34 \times 10^6 = 3.4 \times 10^7$. Dividing the coefficient by $10$ means the index must go up by $1$, not down.

questions.stem: Which of these is $0.06 \times 10^{-4}$ written correctly in standard form?
questions.explanation: $0.06 = 6 \times 10^{-2}$, so $0.06 \times 10^{-4} = 6 \times 10^{-2} \times 10^{-4} = 6 \times 10^{-6}$. Making the coefficient bigger by a factor of $100$ lowers the index by $2$.

questions.stem: Simplify $(4 \times 10^5) + (3 \times 10^4)$, giving your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: Rewrite $3 \times 10^4 = 0.3 \times 10^5$, then add the coefficients: $(4 + 0.3) \times 10^5 = 4.3 \times 10^5$. You cannot add coefficients until the powers of $10$ match.

questions.stem: Simplify $(9 \times 10^{-2}) - (4 \times 10^{-3})$, giving your answer in standard form.
Why must two numbers in standard form be rewritten with the same power of $10$ before they are added?
choices: So that the coefficients count units of the same size.
So that the indices can be added together.
Because standard form answers always use the smaller power.
Because a calculator requires equal powers.
questions.explanation: Each coefficient counts multiples of its own power of $10$. Only when the powers match do the coefficients count the same-sized units, so adding them makes sense.

questions.stem: A rectangular solar farm is $4 \times 10^3$ m long and $2.5 \times 10^2$ m wide. What is its area in standard form?
questions.explanation: $(4 \times 2.5) \times 10^{3+2} = 10 \times 10^5$, and a coefficient of $10$ is not allowed, so adjust to $1 \times 10^6$ m$^2$.

questions.stem: A grant of £6 \times 10^9 is shared equally among $3 \times 10^7$ people. How much does each person receive?
questions.explanation: $(6 \div 3) \times 10^{9-7} = 2 \times 10^2$, so each person receives £2 \times 10^2, which is £200.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is NOT in standard form?
questions.explanation: The coefficient must satisfy $1 \leq a < 10$. Since $0.9 < 1$, the number $0.9 \times 10^7$ is not in standard form; it should be $9 \times 10^6$.

questions.stem: Using standard form with each number rounded to $1$ significant figure, which is the best estimate of $0.000\,078 \times 6\,500\,000$?
questions.explanation: $0.000\,078 \approx 8 \times 10^{-5}$ and $6\,500\,000 \approx 7 \times 10^6$, so the product is about $56 \times 10^1 = 5.6 \times 10^2 \approx 560$. The exact answer, $507$, confirms this is sensible.
